hook_text: In 1889 one cheque bought a diamond empire. Who wrote it, and who lost?
clip_script: Kimberley in the 1880s. Two rivals. Cecil Rhodes, a vicar's son who started out pumping water from flooded mines. Barney Barnato, a comedian from London's East End who arrived with a box of cigars. Rhodes owns the De Beers Mine. Barnato owns most of the Kimberley Mine, the richest of all. Too many diamonds are pushing prices down, and both men know: whoever controls all the mines controls the price. Rhodes gets the mighty Rothschild bank behind him. He buys a company with claims inside Barnato's mine, swaps it for a fifth of Barnato's company, then buys share after share. Barnato gives in. 1888: De Beers Consolidated Mines. 1889: a cheque for over five million pounds. Nine out of every ten diamonds on earth now belong to one company, and Rhodes turns that money towards an empire in the north.
visual_style: A whiteboard split screen of two portraits, a pump and a cigar box, then a tug of war over a mine, a bank vault opening, and a giant cheque being signed.
pacing: Quick cuts between the two men, building to the signature.
